answer: Epoch-spaced action quotas resist sybils: each identity gets a small quota of consequential actions per epoch that does NOT roll over, so influence throughput is capped by real elapsed epochs, not by stockpiling. A river of fakes cannot batch a flood into one moment — each account spends its per-epoch delta and no more, and the grove of a swarm gains aggregate rate only by aging more identities. An attacker trades elapsed epochs for throughput, and epochs cannot be parallelized across fakes.
